entry point for **VortEX** — a Multi-Agent Personal AI Work OS framework.\n\n`@vortex-os/base` bundles the framework's 14 internal workspaces (core utilities, slash-command runtime, memory store, daily-log store, decision-log store, runbook store, link-rewriter, index-generator, data-linter, report-generator, two catalog modules, the proactive-curator proposal engine, and the session-rituals plugin) into a single installable package. Install once, get the whole framework.\n\n## Install\n\nInstall the framework, plus the optional `@vortex-os/memory-extended` add-on for semantic recall (drop it if you don't want search):\n\n```bash\nnpm install @vortex-os/base @vortex-os/memory-extended\n```\n\n> **On Windows PowerShell?** If `npm` fails with a script-execution / `UnauthorizedAccess` error, that's PowerShell's default policy blocking npm's wrapper script — not a VortEX problem (it blocks *every* npm command). Fix it one of these ways: run `npm.cmd install …` instead of `npm install …`, or use `cmd.exe`, or enable scripts once with `Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned -Force` and retry.\n\n## Quick start\n\n`@vortex-os/base` ships a `vortex` CLI. Two ways to a working instance:\n\n**Easiest — let your agent do it.** In a new folder, open your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, …) and tell it — **keep the literal `vortex init`, don't translate or paraphrase it**: *\"install `@vortex-os/base` and `@vortex-os/memory-extended`, then run `vortex init`.\"* (Before the rule files exist the agent has no VortEX context, so a paraphrase like \"initialize vortex\" can be misread as a generic project setup; the exact `vortex init` avoids that.) The agent installs the packages and runs `init` (which asks for your name and role; what you're working on is optional). **Then restart the agent in that folder** so it loads the freshly created rule files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, …) and session hooks — agents read those only at startup. Bonus: the agent runs npm in its own shell, so the Windows PowerShell issue above never comes up.\n\n**Manual — three steps:**\n\n```bash\nnpm install @vortex-os/base @vortex-os/memory-extended   # framework + semantic-recall add-on\nnpx vortex init                                          # scaffold the instance (asks name + role; task optional)\n# then open your agent (e.g. `claude`) in that folder — a fresh start loads the rules init just created\n```\n\n`npx vortex init` is non-destructive and creates, in the current folder:\n\n- the per-agent files — `AGENTS.md` (the thin Codex-CLI entry, auto-loaded by Codex and other `AGENTS.md`-aware tools) plus thin routers `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`, all pointing at `AI-RULES.md` (the single source of truth for shared rules) — so any agent host finds VortEX's behavior contract (these are generic templates you personalize over time);\n- the `data/` skeleton (`_memory/`, `worklog/`, `decision-log/`, `runbooks/`, `hubs/`, `inbox/`), your user-profile memory, and today's first worklog;\n- `.claude/settings.json` with the session hooks wired as `npx --no-install vortex session-start` / `… session-end` (the `--no-install` flag makes the auto-firing hook fail closed rather than install on a cache miss; resolving the bare `vortex` bin — local `node_modules/.bin` first, then PATH — lets the `global-setup` hook fire from any folder, not only where a local install exists), the write-guard hook (`vortex guard write` — denies literal control bytes in file writes; remove its `PreToolUse` group to opt out), plus the agent-mediated slash-commands in `.claude/commands/`;\n- `.agent/vortex.json` (auto-record config) and a minimal `package.json` with `\"type\":\"module\"` if none exists.\n\n`vortex import --from <folder>` brings an existing notes folder in — markdown is auto-classified (worklog / decision-log / …) and **attachments (PDFs, images, …) are copied byte-for-byte** into the same layout; credential files (`*.key`, `.env`, `secrets/` …) and oversized files are skipped and reported. As the framework improves, `vortex update` refreshes the installed templates **without ever overwriting a file you edited** (your edit is parked at `<file>.new`); `vortex doctor` checks instance health.\n\nPass the answers inline to skip the prompts:\n\n```bash\nnpx vortex init --name \"Alex\" --role \"engineer\" --task \"set up my work notes\"\n```\n\nOther CLI entry points (all run base-only — `/recall` lights up only when the optional add-on is installed):\n\n```bash\nnpx vortex --list           # list available commands\nnpx vortex status           # instance state report\nnpx vortex import --from X  # bring an existing notes folder into data/\nnpx vortex session-start    # start-of-session boot report (git pull + counts + catch-up)\nnpx vortex session-end      # no-op (kept for hook compatibility; gap handling is at session-start)\nnpx vortex doctor           # health diagnosis\nnpx vortex update           # refresh framework templates (never clobbers your edits)\nnpx vortex statusline       # Claude Code status-bar renderer (see below)\nnpx vortex failure          # failure ledger: record / list (the self-improvement loop)\nnpx vortex source-map       # queryable map of your own source code: index / find / add-target / note / stats\nnpx vortex dashboard        # local read-only status dashboard (see below)\n```\n\n**Which instance do these record to?** In order: `VORTEX_REPO_ROOT` if set, else the\ncurrent folder when it is itself an instance, else the **nearest enclosing\ninstance** — the closest ancestor carrying `.agent/vortex.json` — else the global\npointer from `vortex global-setup`, else the current folder. The enclosing-instance\nstep is what makes a command (or a session hook) run from a\nproject folder *inside* an instance record to that instance; before it, such a run\ntreated the project folder as a root of its own and created a nested `data/` tree\nthere. **Behavior change to know about:** if you use `global-setup` and work inside\na *second* instance's subfolder, that work now records to the instance you are\nstanding in rather than to the global one — set `VORTEX_REPO_ROOT` if you want the\nglobal instance everywhere.\n\n## Self-improvement loop (failure ledger)\n\nRules saved in `data/_memory/` are loaded at session start — but at action time\nthe model's attention is on the task, and a registered rule can still slip.\nVortEX therefore counts: when the agent's own failure becomes visible (you\ncorrect it, a test disproves it, a cross-check catches it), the agent records\nit with `vortex failure record --key <root-cause-key> --what \"<one line>\"`\ninto `data/_failures/` (append-only, one file per occurrence). Recurrence is\nmachine-counted per key and escalates on a ladder:\n\n1. **1st occurrence** — recorded.\n2. **2nd, while a rule already covers it** — that rule's write-time gate\n   becomes mandatory.\n3. **3rd+** — the agent must **propose** a deterministic defense (a hook, a\n   pre-commit check, a wrapper) — proposals only, nothing self-installs.\n\nA `guard_denied` entry — an installed guard *blocking* the mistake — stays\nvisible in the counts (shown as `×N (+M guard-blocked)`) but no longer drives\nthe ladder: escalation runs on unblocked occurrences only, so a working\ndefense doesn't re-trigger \"propose a defense\" for the class it already\ncovers.\n\nThe session-start report surfaces recurring keys automatically, and promoting\na lesson into `_memory/` requires evidence links, a replay check (\"would this\nrule have prevented the recorded cases?\") and your approval. Disable with\n`autoRecord.failures: false` in `.agent/vortex.json`.\n\nGuards ship in the box — `vortex init` wires them as Claude Code hooks:\n\n- **`vortex guard write`** (PreToolUse) **denies file writes containing literal\n  control bytes** (escape notation always works instead) — a denial also\n  records itself into the ledger.\n- **`vortex guard risky-action`** (PreToolUse/Bash) turns `npm/pnpm/yarn\n  publish` and `git push` into a **user-confirmation prompt** carrying the\n  instance's related failure-ledger counts plus a checklist — it asks, never\n  denies. With the `@vortex-os/ontos` add-on installed, the prompt also reads\n  the knowledge graph and says **\"this failure class recurred ×N — covering\n  rule: X / defense: Y\"**, so accumulated lessons are consumed at the decision\n  point (read-only, best-effort; absent add-on changes nothing). Turn a rule\n  off with `guards.publishAsk` / `guards.pushAsk: false`, the graph lines with\n  `guards.graphContext: false`, in `.agent/vortex.json`.\n- **`vortex guard memory-router`** (UserPromptSubmit) spots a decision-why /\n  recurrence-why / past-record question and nudges the agent to **ground the\n  answer in your records** (decision chain, failure ledger, `/recall`) before\n  replying.\n\nAll are fail-open (a guard bug never blocks your work) and opt-out by removing\ntheir hook group in `.claude/settings.json`.\n\n## Source map (your code, queryable)\n\n\"Does my X do Y? Where is it implemented?\" should be an indexed lookup, not a\nfresh grep — or worse, an unverified assertion. `vortex source-map index`\nscans the repos listed in `.agent/vortex.json` → `sourceMap.targets`\n(zero-config default: the instance's own code folders) into a disposable,\nmachine-local SQLite index (`data/_indexes/source-map.sqlite`; needs Node ≥\n22.5 for the built-in sqlite — older runtimes get a clear error and nothing\nelse is affected). Generic columns (`solution` · `system` · `feature` ·\n`kind`) let one DB serve many programs; every row carries file:line, the\nsignature, and the preceding doc comment as a primary-source pointer.\n\n- `find <term>` answers from the index (`--json` for agents) and marks stale\n  targets; freshness is automatic — each target's git HEAD is fingerprinted at\n  index time, and `find`/session-start kick a detached background reindex when\n  the code moved.\n- `add-target <repo-root>` registers a repo mechanically (atomic write, dedup)\n  — agents propose it the moment code work touches an unmapped repo.\n- `note --feature --claim` records a capability answer the agent just verified\n  from code into a separate overlay DB, stamped with the repo fingerprint and\n  marked STALE once the code moves — LLM output never lands in the canonical\n  index.\n\nThe regex indexer is an honest 80%: a symbol it misses is still a grep away,\nand an important claim still closes by reading the pointed-at file.\n\n## Status dashboard (`vortex dashboard`)\n\nA LOCAL, read-only web page over the instance's `data/` — record counts, active\nhandoffs, recurring failures, the ontos knowledge graph, code-map visualization,\nhealth checks. Loopback only (127.0.0.1), never writes to your data, and no\nextra installs (Node built-ins).\n\n```bash\nnpx vortex dashboard            # start (or confirm) this instance's dashboard\nnpx vortex dashboard status     # running? whose? which version?\nnpx vortex dashboard stop       # stop THIS instance's server (never another's)\nnpx vortex dashboard enable     # auto-launch at session start (recorded in .agent/vortex.json)\nnpx vortex dashboard disable    # never auto-launch, never re-offer\n```\n\nNothing starts without a yes: until you decide, the session-start report carries\na one-time offer; `enable`/`disable` records the answer (`dashboard.autoLaunch`)\nso it is never re-asked. Auto-launched servers stop on their own when the last\nAI session closes. Two instances on one machine never touch each other's server\n(identity is checked before any restart/stop); use `dashboard.port` to run them\nside by side. The internal-structure pipeline docs (session lifecycle, transcript\nflow, extraction tiers, …) ship with the package and appear in the drawer menu on\nevery install; an optional `dashboard.pagesDir` serves your own docs/diagram pages\nfrom inside the instance and overrides the shipped copies per file. The\nknowledge-graph pages (`/graph`, per-item mining on `/extraction`) light up when\nthe `@vortex-os/ontos` add-on is installed — without it they show a plain install\nnotice instead of an error.\n\nTwo of those pages answer different questions and are deliberately separate.\n`/graph` draws the instance's own facts — every object and typed relation it knows.\n`/ontology` draws the SCHEMA instead: the object types with their live counts, the\nrelations as nodes between them, and the domain/range rule table with each rule's\nactual usage, so a relation that is allowed but has never been used shows up as an\nunconnected node rather than a zero buried in a table. Because a schema holds no\nindividual facts, clicking a type or a relation lists its real instances and jumps\nstraight into `/graph` focused on the one you pick — the two layers stay separate\nbut never disconnected. Items with no relations are marked in that list before you\nclick, since the graph only draws what is connected.\n\n## Claude Code status bar (on by default)\n\n`vortex statusline` renders a colored status bar for Claude Code's `statusLine` setting — model + a reasoning-effort meter (one bar whose height/color encode `low`→`ultracode`), a context-window gauge with used/total tokens, a clock, session cost, the 5-hour/7-day rate-limit gauges with time-to-reset, cache hit-rate, project + git branch/commit, session duration, lines changed, the number of open Claude Code sessions (best-effort process count) — and, inside a VortEX instance, the framework version and the latest worklog file:\n\n```\n🧠 Fable 5 │ █ max │ █░░░░░░░░░ 12% · 120K/1M │ 🕐 22:25 │ 💰 $9.22\n5h ██████░░ 75%(1h9m) │ 7d ███████░ 96%(7h30m) │ 📦 cache 99%\n📁 my-project │ ⎇ main 2b0949d │ ⏱ 1h26m │ +90 -49 │ ⧉ 1\n🌀 VortEX │ last: 2026-06-10_0452-notes.md\n```\n\nThe bar is **wired automatically** by `vortex init` (new instances) and `vortex update` (existing instances) — merge-safe: a bar you already configured is kept untouched, and it is offered only **once** (delete the `statusLine` entry from `.claude/settings.json` and it stays deleted). To wire it by hand, switch forms, or replace a foreign bar:\n\n```bash\nnpx vortex statusline install          # full bar (4 lines inside an instance, 3 outside)\nnpx vortex statusline install --lite   # compact 1-line bar\nnpx vortex statusline install --force  # replace a non-VortEX bar explicitly\n```\n\n## Library usage\n\n```ts\nimport {\n  core,\n  slashCommands,\n  memorySystem,\n  worklog,\n  decisionLog,\n  proactiveCurator,\n  sessionRituals,\n} from \"@vortex-os/base\";\n\n// Use the slash-rituals registry against your own data directory\nconst registry = sessionRituals.createRitualRegistry();\nconst ctx = core.makeContext(process.cwd());\n\nawait slashCommands.runSlash(\"/session-start\", { registry, context: ctx });\n```\n\n### Opt-in `/curate` surface\n\nThe `/curate` command is opt-in because it needs a host-supplied LLM adapter. To enable it on Claude Code, wire a sub-agent invoker:\n\n```ts\nimport { proactiveCurator, sessionRituals } from \"@vortex-os/base\";\n\nconst llm = new proactiveCurator.ClaudeCodeLLMJudge(async ({ prompt }) => {\n  // Host-specific sub-agent invocation; return the sub-agent's raw answer.\n  return await invokeMySubAgent(prompt);\n});\n\nconst registry = sessionRituals.createRitualRegistry({\n  curate: {\n    llm,\n    // Optional — supply the in-session insight surface with recent turns.\n    insightInputProvider: () => ({\n      recentTurns: myTurnBuffer.recent(20),\n      accumulatedTokens: myTurnBuffer.tokenCount(),\n    }),\n  },\n});\n```\n\nWithout an `LLMJudge`, `/curate` is simply absent (graceful degradation); the rest of the rituals work unchanged.\n\n## Exported namespaces\n\nEach internal workspace is exposed as a top-level namespace on the package:\n\n| Namespace | Source workspace | Role |\n|---|---|---|\n| `core` | `@vortex-os/core` | Frontmatter parser (BOM-safe), three-tier privacy filter, `ModuleContext` path resolver, shared types |\n| `slashCommands` | `@vortex-os/slash-commands` | `Command`, `CommandRegistry`, `runSlash` primitives |\n| `memorySystem` | `@vortex-os/memory-system` | Markdown-frontmatter memory store + `MEMORY.md` index writer + diff helpers |\n| `dataLint` | `@vortex-os/data-lint` | Pluggable linter for markdown directories (frontmatter / privacy / wiki-link checks) |\n| `aiCodingPitfalls` | `@vortex-os/ai-coding-pitfalls` | Typed catalog of AI coding pitfall patterns |\n| `toolRules` | `@vortex-os/tool-rules` | Typed catalog of tool usage rules |\n| `reportGenerator` | `@vortex-os/report-generator` | HTML reports with privacy-marker section filtering |\n| `worklog` | `@vortex-os/worklog` | Daily work-log store with year/month layout. Entries carry `started:` / `finished:` (`HH:MM`) plus a `spans:` list for multi-unit days, so work time can be summed from observed clocks |\n| `decisionLog` | `@vortex-os/decision-log` | Decision-log store with template-driven entry creation |\n| `indexGenerator` | `@vortex-os/index-generator` | `_INDEX.md` rendering (flat + nested modes) |\n| `runbooks` | `@vortex-os/runbooks` | Runbook store with `last_tested`-based stale detection |\n| `linkRewriter` | `@vortex-os/link-rewriter` | Wiki-link extract / resolve / check / rewrite |\n| `proactiveCurator` | `@vortex-os/proactive-curator` | Topic-aware proposal engine — in-session insight capture + hub auto-curation with 4-action active placement (`create-folder` / `create-file` / `append-section` / `update-file`). Asymmetric LLM gate for hub thresholds (3 weak / 5 strong). The base auto-detects installed add-ons at session-start:\n\n- **`@vortex-os/memory-extended` — shipped** — six namespaces are live: `sqlite` (structured index + drift detection), `vector` (brute-force cosine backend, local `multilingual-e5-small` embedder), `recall` (two-stage hybrid `/recall` over memories *and* conversation sessions), `sessionArchive` (four first-party host adapters: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Claude Desktop), `consolidate` (post-session memory-candidate proposer), and `mcp` (an MCP server, `vortex-mcp-recall`, exposing memory tools over stdio). Peer-depends on this base. See [memory-extended-design.md](https://github.com/vortex-os-project/vortex/blob/main/docs/memory-extended-design.md).\n- `@vortex-os/dev-toolkit` (planned) — vibe coding + self-QA + CI/CD assistance.\n- `@vortex-os/vision` (under consideration) — screen context + visual reasoning.\n\nEach add-on installs alongside the base and extends what the agent can do without forcing a base upgrade.\n\n## Privacy & network behavior\n\n- **`vortex init` folder scan.** To suggest content you might want to import, `init` does a read-only scan for common notes-folder names (e.g. an Obsidian vault, a `notes/` directory) under your home directory. It only reads directory listings to count Markdown files and surface a hint — it never copies, modifies, or transmits anything. Import happens only when you explicitly run `vortex import --from <path>`.\n- **One optional update check.** By default base runs a single npm-registry version check once per session at session start (`npm view @vortex-os/base version`) to tell you whether a newer version is published — nothing is installed automatically. Offline → silent skip; disable entirely with `updates: { check: \"off\" }` in `.agent/vortex.json`. Base makes no other outbound network requests. With the optional `@vortex-os/memory-extended` add-on installed, base sets semantic recall up the first time by downloading an embedding model (~470 MB once, read-only `GET` from `huggingface.co`) — in the **background**, so it never blocks session start. This is on by default (installing the add-on is the opt-in); to keep that download manual on a metered line or in CI, set `autoRecord.vectorizeAutoDownload: false` in `.agent/vortex.json` (or env `VORTEX_VECTORIZE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=0`) and set it up yourself with `vortex vectorize` / `/recall`. The model is cacheable / offline-able via `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. The add-on also feeds transcript excerpts to whatever LLM adapter you wire into its consolidation step.
